newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 10.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:

* LONDON - British Sky Broadcasting has ended its alliance with the Kirch Group to develop digital satellite television in Germany. The break-up is a blow to BSkyB's plans to expand into continental Europe and to Kirch's DF1 digital platform. BSkyB was supposed to be taking a stake of up to 49 percent in DF1. BSkyB's largest shareholder is News Corp.

* HOLLYWOOD - "Private Parts" by Viacom's Paramount brought in $15.1 million, including roughly $800,000 from Thursday previews, to make its way to first place in the weekend box office. "Jungle 2 Jungle" from Disney was close behind with an estimated $12.7 million. "Private Parts" came in with a $6,690 average from 2,138 prints during its weekend debut.

* WASHINGTON - Under pressure from Capitol Hill, several TV industry lobbyists now want to modify the program-rating system so that it provides more info about the sexual and violent content of a program. Talks are still in the preliminary stages, but sources said industry representatives are reacting to the negative reviews the rating system received Feb. 27 during a Senate hearing.

* HOLLYWOOD - "The English Patient" continued its drive to the Oscars over the weekend, as first-time nominee Anthony Minghella won the Directors Guild of America Award. Given the DGA's track record as a precursor, "Patient" becomes a favorite for the Oscars. It already has won a Golden Globe for dramatic picture and other honors.

* NEW YORK - Robin Williams will co-star with Matt Damon and Ben Affleck in Gus Van Sant's drama "Good Will Hunting," which Disney's Miramax Films will begin shooting next month in Boston and Toronto. The movie tells the story of a troubled prodigy who comes from the wrong side of the tracks.

* ORLANDO, Fla - Bertelsmann Music Group North America has won the hotly contested bidding war for distribution rights to Richard Branson's V2 Records. The multiyear deal, which closed late last week, is an enormous feather in BMG's cap, especially considering the conglom bested overtures from Polygram and WEA, the industry's leading distributor, which handles releases for Warner Music Group.
